title: Principal Software Engineer
shortDesc: Architected and built a 12-repository, multi-service platform in Rust and Python — 406 commits, 135,000+ lines of application code, 37 REST and WebSocket endpoints, and two production-shaped data pipelines including a cited, locally-run large language model (LLM) retrieval-augmented generation system measured against a 130-question held-out evaluation set.
longDesc: Designed and delivered the ThreatLVL platform end to end: a shared rules-engine library consumed by five services, a 26-route Actix-web API gateway with WebSocket subscriptions, an RS256 OIDC (OpenID Connect) authentication service backed by PostgreSQL and Redis, a GitOps deployment repository running under Kubernetes and ArgoCD, and two independent ingestion pipelines. Worked from written specifications throughout — 15 design proposals with high-level and low-level detail, a decisions log tracking 19 open questions with options and constraints, and 17 numbered architecture revisions — translating product requirements into technical designs before implementation. Enforced object-oriented and type-driven design patterns across a 3,250-file workspace with compile-time modularity: 17 build features and 17,642 conditional-compilation sites let each service compile only the subsystems it needs, sized against a deliberately constrained reference machine. Practiced disciplined defect triage and root cause analysis on machine-generated data — tracing 22 license misclassifications, a challenge-rating experience-point calculation bug, a cross-edition index leak, and 56 CSV rows damaged by a quoting defect back to their causes and fixing the tooling so each class of failure could not recur. Built the generative AI surface as an engineering system under explicit AI governance: a four-stage Python document pipeline feeding large language models (LLM) retrieval-augmented generation with mandatory citation and provenance, retrieval abstracted behind a single swappable interface with both a lexical (SQLite FTS5/BM25) and an embedding-based lane, prompt engineering via prompt templates read from version control at runtime so documented and executed prompts cannot drift, capped and time-bounded local model inference on CPU-only hardware, a 130-question held-out evaluation set, and a standing architectural rule that no AI-dependent path may block the user or run without a deterministic fallback.

blurbs.Software Engineer: Architected a multi-service platform (microservices) in Rust across 12 repositories and 406 commits, applying object-oriented and type-driven software design patterns, data-structure and algorithm work, and compile-time modularity (17 build features, 17,642 conditional-compilation sites) as part of a disciplined systems design practice. Produced high-level and low-level technical design documentation before implementation — 15 written proposals with open questions resolved in writing, a 19-question decisions log, and 17 numbered architecture revisions — including reversing an edition-split architecture after the evidence showed it cost more than it returned. Held a hard quality baseline: zero-warning linting, enforced formatting, and a five-variant compile matrix required before any commit touching the core system module.
blurbs.Back End: Built five backend services in Rust on Actix-web, exposing a REST API and WebSocket surface: a 26-route API gateway with WebSocket subscriptions, room and invitation lifecycle, message and notes APIs with per-role authorization filtering, and player heartbeats; an authentication service issuing RS256 JSON Web Tokens (JWT) as an OIDC provider with Argon2 password hashing, PostgreSQL persistence via SQL, and Redis caching; plus static-content and server-rendered web services, and a WebAssembly (WASM)-compiled Leptos client consuming the gateway directly from the browser. Designed the canonical shared library every microservice consumes and none reimplements. Engineered the AI surface as a backend concern — retrieval behind one swappable interface, model calls capped and time-bounded, prompts loaded from version-controlled files at runtime, and a deterministic fallback required on every AI-dependent path. Load-tested the gateway on constrained reference hardware, found the per-user connection pool failed near six concurrent users, and replaced it with a stateless per-request design — the fix removed 673 lines and added 256.
blurbs.Data: Built and operated two ETL (extract/transform/load) pipelines over licensed third-party content, 20 Python modules and 4,932 lines across the ingestion toolchain, with data modeling for a 20+ entity-type relational schema. The first generates typed, license-classified code from three upstream datasets, with per-row classification against two specification versions, a 164-entry alias layer resolving cross-source naming conflicts, and proven idempotency against a merged baseline. The second is a four-stage document pipeline — extraction with 14 per-publisher layout strategies, rules-first shape classification, indexing, and evaluation — converting publisher PDFs into provenance-tagged chunks across 19 books and 2,950 chunks, serving citation-bearing answers from a locally-run model. Designed retrieval as a swappable backend rather than a committed dependency: one entry point, a SQLite FTS5/BM25 full-text search lexical lane as the default and an implemented vector search embedding lane (nomic-embed-text, 768-dimension vectors, brute-force cosine), with the choice to defer sqlite-vec documented against its real cost — regenerating a hash-locked lockfile and moving a supply-chain security `exclude-newer` cutoff. Ran model evaluation rather than asserting quality with a 130-question held-out evaluation set across 13 books, reproducible runs, and stage-to-stage count-agreement assertions that fail loudly on silent data loss. Root-caused and fixed 22 license misclassifications, a calculation bug, a cross-edition index leak, and 56 quote-damaged rows, hardening the tooling against each.
blurbs.Administrator: Maintained a 3,250-file, 12-repository workspace as one coherent system: zero-tolerance lint and format gates, a five-variant per-edition compile matrix before every core-module commit, warning count driven from 2,518 to 2,032, and 437 files brought into format compliance in a single pass. Ran the tracking substrate that made a 1,592-item campaign finishable — a 2,901-row object inventory, status accounting, and ingest logs, with unresolved items error-logged rather than dropped. Managed submodule pointer hygiene across seven submodules, dependency-path migrations, and filename-convention migrations across hundreds of files without data loss. Applied supply-chain controls as policy: hash-pinned dependencies with a time-based cutoff, authenticated dependency clones in continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD), Docker-containerized services deployed via Kubernetes and ArgoCD (GitOps), and pre-commit controls preventing licensed content from entering version control.
blurbs.Consulting: Ran the engagement so that nothing significant was decided in passing: a decisions log carrying 19 numbered open questions with context, options, constraints, and a locked / open / parked status — including items deliberately parked rather than resolved prematurely. Established a proposal → review → decision → bake-in workflow, with applied proposals removed so the staging area never misrepresented what was live. Produced stakeholder-actionable artifacts: a phased roadmap, competitive positioning, a business model with licensing posture, and storage-tier tradeoffs marked locked or provisional. Evaluated emerging technology against measured cost rather than reputation — deferring a vector-database dependency after pricing it against a millisecond-scale brute-force scan and a supply-chain cutoff it would have forced. Flagged discovered inconsistencies with evidence for triage instead of fixing them unilaterally.
blurbs.Team Lead: Built the onboarding surface a second engineer would need before there was one: 118 documents totaling 54,930 lines — contributor guides, per-service tactical guides layered under a strategic source of truth, implementer playbooks written for someone absent from the design conversation, runbooks, and procedures. Defined standards and enforced them mechanically rather than socially. Ran multi-agent AI orchestration with written agent specifications, pass tracking, and status accounting to drive batch work across thousands of generated files, with automated formatting and zero-warning linting as the gate every batch had to clear.

title: Lead DevOps & Full-Stack Engineer
shortDesc: Architected CI/CD (continuous integration/continuous deployment) pipelines, Kubernetes platform infrastructure, per-patient encryption, and a full Firebase-to-PostgreSQL migration for an AI-powered clinical avatar platform, then closed the 10-week engagement with penetration testing remediation and hardened production containers.
longDesc: Joined a healthcare AI startup with no CI/CD, no production infrastructure, and a Firebase-based data layer, and delivered a production-ready platform in 10 weeks across 604 commits. Designed and built an 11-workflow GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline spanning 6 environments with blue-green production deployments, SHA-verified staging approval, and runtime environment injection (build once, deploy anywhere); created the Kubernetes/EKS platform infrastructure from Helm charts through production hardening; led the complete Firebase-to-PostgreSQL migration (25-table schema, Drizzle ORM, a 115-file repository abstraction layer); implemented per-patient column-level encryption with cryptographic audit-log hash chains and WORM export to S3 Object Lock; built GDPR/HIPAA compliance features including data exports, automated retention enforcement, and PHI audit logging across 32 API routes; optimized database performance with UUIDv7 primary keys, N+1 elimination, and GIN-indexed JSONB queries; introduced conventional commits with semantic versioning; closed the engagement by remediating a full penetration-test report (CSPRNG, authentication guards on 7 PHI endpoints, Postgres-backed rate limiting, input validation) and shipping a distroless production image with 96% fewer container vulnerabilities. Ran the engagement against a written PHI security requirements document and a 19-item decision log tracking every deferred or resolved compliance gap, moving the internal compliance audit score from 58% to 82% (zero critical code gaps) across two review passes.

blurbs.Administrator: Managed an AWS EKS cluster across every environment: emergency scaling (20GB to 100GB EBS with no service interruption), PostgreSQL TLS in transit via cert-manager, nginx ingress controller configuration, database credential hardening with role separation, vendor-agnostic backup infrastructure (pg_dump + WAL-G via rclone), a login-healthcheck CronJob with Discord API alerting, bash automation scripts for deploy/rollback/status operations, admin user management with approver role gates, and Kubernetes NetworkPolicies for pod-traffic isolation. Handed off infrastructure-only remediation items (S3 bucket-level SSE, backup GPG encryption, etcd encryption at rest) explicitly to the infrastructure admin rather than absorbing them into application-code scope.
blurbs.Back End: Led a complete Firebase-to-PostgreSQL migration with Drizzle ORM on a Node.js runtime: designed a 25-table multi-tenant architecture, built a repository abstraction layer (115 files), implemented per-patient column-level AES-256 encryption, cryptographic audit-log hash chains, PHI audit logging across 32 routes, UUIDv7 primary keys, N+1 query elimination, GIN-indexed JSONB queries, server-side pagination, compile-time branded types (PatientId, ClinicianId, CoachId, ClinicId, FlowId), CSPRNG access-code generation, Postgres-backed distributed rate limiting, authentication guards on 7 previously unauthenticated PHI endpoints, HMAC-SHA256 signature verification on deployment webhooks, and per-request database/S3 routing serving 3 production subdomains from a single image.
blurbs.Business: Implemented per-patient encryption and cryptographic audit-log hash chains with WORM export to S3 Object Lock for tamper-evident compliance proof. Built GDPR data export with a CI verification gate and automated retention enforcement for EU market operation. Closed a penetration-test report across OWASP-relevant categories and achieved a 96% container-vulnerability reduction via distroless images. Moved a PHI compliance audit score from 58% to 82% (zero critical code gaps) across two review passes in as many days.
blurbs.Consulting: Joined an engagement with no CI/CD and no production infrastructure, assessed the architecture, and executed 604 commits across CI/CD, Kubernetes, database migration, per-patient encryption, and compliance audit infrastructure in 10 weeks. Maintained a 19-item decision log (owner, status, rationale per gap — Engineering / Business / Legal / Admin) so nothing was decided in passing, and explicitly separated infrastructure-admin work from application-code scope. Closed the engagement with a distroless production image and penetration-test remediation as the final deliverables, leaving the codebase in a stable, documented state.
blurbs.Data: Designed a 25-table PostgreSQL schema with per-patient column-level encryption and legal-hold support. Migrated primary keys to UUIDv7, eliminated N+1 queries with batched lookups, replaced full-table scans with GIN-indexed JSONB queries, tuned the connection pool for thousands of sessions per hour, and built vendor-agnostic backup infrastructure (pg_dump + WAL-G via rclone, portable across S3/GCS/Azure/MinIO). Tracked session recordings in the database for O(1) GDPR export lookups instead of an S3 list scan.
blurbs.DevOps: Built the CI/CD and platform-engineering surface from zero: an 11-workflow GitHub Actions pipeline (continuous integration/continuous deployment) across 6 environments, blue-green production deployments with multi-host ingress and SHA-verified staging approval, automated feature-branch preview environments with TLS and teardown, runtime environment injection (build once, deploy anywhere), a distroless production Docker image cutting container vulnerabilities 96%, conventional commits with semantic versioning and an approver-editable CHANGELOG, GHCR image-retention policy, and a login-healthcheck CronJob with Discord alerting.

blurbs.Software Engineer: Shipped 604 commits over a 10-week engagement spanning CI/CD architecture, Kubernetes infrastructure, a Firebase-to-PostgreSQL migration (698 files touched, +187,549/-71,550 lines of churn), per-patient encryption with cryptographic audit chains, GDPR/HIPAA compliance features, UUIDv7 migration, blue-green deployments, conventional commits with semantic versioning, penetration-test remediation (CSPRNG, auth hardening, rate limiting, input validation), and distroless container hardening (96% fewer CVEs) — all in TypeScript strict mode.
